title: Classical Thermodynamics (First Law, Work, Heat, Internal Energy, Enthalpy, & Hess's Law)
syllabus: Fundamentals of thermodynamics: System and surroundings, extensive and intensive properties, state and path functions; First law of thermodynamics: Internal energy (U), heat (q), and work (w); Pressure-volume work in reversible and irreversible isothermal/adiabatic expansions and compressions of ideal gases; Enthalpy (H), relation between ΔH and ΔU (ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT); Heat capacities (C_p, C_v) and their relationship; Thermochemistry: Standard enthalpy changes of reaction, formation, combustion, neutralization, and phase transitions; Hess's Law of constant heat summation and its applications; Bond dissociation enthalpies and lattice enthalpy (Born-Haber cycle)

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly from a volume of $2\text{ L}$ to $20\text{ L}$ at $300\text{ K}$. The work done by the gas in this process is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.303$)
questions.solution:
For an isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, the work done (by IUPAC convention, $w = -\int P_{ext} dV$) is given by:
$$w = -nRT \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right) = -2.303 nRT \log_{10}\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$$
Substitute the given values:
- $n = 2\text{ mol}$
- $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$
- $T = 300\text{ K}$
- $V_1 = 2\text{ L}, \quad V_2 = 20\text{ L} \implies \frac{V_2}{V_1} = 10$

$$w = -2.303 \times 2 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10}(10)$$
$$w = -2.303 \times 2 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 1 = -11488.5\text{ J} \approx -11.49\text{ kJ}$$
(The negative sign indicates work is done by the system on the surroundings).

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2022] For the combustion of one mole of liquid benzene at $298\text{ K}$:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6(l) + \frac{15}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 6\text{CO}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
The difference between the enthalpy change and internal energy change ($\Delta H - \Delta U$) in $\text{kJ}$ is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The relation between $\Delta H$ and $\Delta U$ is:
$$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT \implies \Delta H - \Delta U = \Delta n_g RT$$
Calculate $\Delta n_g$ (change in moles of gaseous substances):
$$\Delta n_g = n_g(\text{products}) - n_g(\text{reactants})$$
Here, the gaseous species are $6\text{ mol of CO}_2$ and $\frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ mol of O}_2$ (benzene and water are in liquid state):
$$\Delta n_g = 6 - 7.5 = -1.5$$
Substitute $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $T = 298\text{ K}$:
$$\Delta H - \Delta U = (-1.5) \times 8.314 \times 298\text{ J} = -3716.36\text{ J} \approx -3.72\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A gas expands from a volume of $2.0\text{ L}$ to $6.0\text{ L}$ against a constant external pressure of $2.5\text{ atm}$. During this expansion, it absorbs $600\text{ J}$ of heat from the surroundings. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of the gas is: (Take $1\text{ L}\cdot\text{atm} = 101.3\text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
Work done in an irreversible expansion against a constant external pressure is:
$$w = -P_{ext} \Delta V = -2.5\text{ atm} \times (6.0 - 2.0)\text{ L} = -2.5 \times 4.0 = -10.0\text{ L}\cdot\text{atm}$$
Convert work to Joules:
$$w = -10.0 \times 101.3\text{ J} = -1013\text{ J}$$
Heat absorbed by the system:
$$q = +600\text{ J}$$
According to the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = q + w = 600\text{ J} + (-1013\text{ J}) = -413\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following collections contains ONLY state functions?
questions.solution:
State functions depend only on the current macroscopic state of the system and are independent of the path taken to reach that state.
- Internal energy ($U$), Enthalpy ($H$), Temperature ($T$), Pressure ($P$), Volume ($V$), Entropy ($S$), and Gibbs energy ($G$) are state functions.
- Heat ($q$) and Work ($w$) are path functions because their values depend on the specific path/process followed between states.
Therefore, the group in Option A contains only state functions.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2020] Given the following thermochemical equations:
1) $\text{C}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g); \quad \Delta H_1 = -393.5\text{ kJ/mol}$
2) $\text{H}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l); \quad \Delta H_2 = -285.8\text{ kJ/mol}$
3) $\text{CH}_4(g) + 2\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l); \quad \Delta H_3 = -890.3\text{ kJ/mol}$
The standard enthalpy of formation of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) is:
questions.solution:
The target formation reaction is:
$$\text{C}(s) + 2\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_4(g) \quad (\Delta H_f^\circ)$$
Using Hess's Law:
$$\text{Equation} = \text{Eq (1)} + 2 \times \text{Eq (2)} - \text{Eq (3)}$$
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = \Delta H_1 + 2\Delta H_2 - \Delta H_3$$
Substitute the numeric values:
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = (-393.5) + 2(-285.8) - (-890.3)$$
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = -393.5 - 571.6 + 890.3 = -965.1 + 890.3 = -74.8\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] For an ideal gas undergoing an adiabatic reversible expansion, which of the following relations is correct? ($\gamma = C_p/C_v$)
questions.solution:
For a reversible adiabatic process of an ideal gas ($dq = 0$):
$$dU = dw \implies n C_v dT = -P dV = -\frac{nRT}{V} dV$$
$$\frac{C_v}{R} \frac{dT}{T} = -\frac{dV}{V}$$
Since $R = C_p - C_v$ and $\gamma = C_p/C_v$, we have $\frac{R}{C_v} = \gamma - 1$.
Integrating yields:
$$\ln T + (\gamma - 1)\ln V = \text{constant} \implies T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$$
The other standard equivalent relations are $P V^\gamma = \text{constant}$ and $T^\gamma P^{1 - \gamma} = \text{constant}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas ($\gamma = 5/3$) at $300\text{ K}$ is subjected to a free expansion in an isolated chamber from $10\text{ L}$ to $50\text{ L}$. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) and the final temperature are:
questions.solution:
In free expansion into a vacuum, the external pressure is zero ($P_{ext} = 0$), so:
$$w = -\int P_{ext} dV = 0$$
Since the container is isolated, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings:
$$q = 0$$
From the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = q + w = 0 + 0 = 0$$
For an ideal gas, internal energy is solely a function of temperature: $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.
Since $\Delta U = 0$, we have $\Delta T = 0$, which means:
$$T_f = T_i = 300\text{ K}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The bond dissociation enthalpies of $\text{H}-\text{H}$, $\text{Cl}-\text{Cl}$, and $\text{H}-\text{Cl}$ are $434$, $242$, and $431\text{ kJ/mol}$ respectively. The standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{HCl}(g)$ is:
questions.solution:
The formation reaction of $\text{HCl}(g)$ for 1 mole of product is:
$$\frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{HCl}(g)$$
Using bond dissociation energies:
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = \sum \text{B.E.}(\text{reactants broken}) - \sum \text{B.E.}(\text{products formed})$$
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = \left[\frac{1}{2}\text{B.E.}(\text{H}-\text{H}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{B.E.}(\text{Cl}-\text{Cl})\right] - \text{B.E.}(\text{H}-\text{Cl})$$
Substitute the values:
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = \left[\frac{1}{2}(434) + \frac{1}{2}(242)\right] - 431$$
$$\Delta H_f^\circ = [217 + 121] - 431 = 338 - 431 = -93\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process $A \rightarrow B \rightarrow C \rightarrow A$. If the heat absorbed along $A \rightarrow B$ is $50\text{ J}$, work done along $B \rightarrow C$ is $-20\text{ J}$, and process $C \rightarrow A$ is adiabatic with work done $+30\text{ J}$, the total work done in the entire cycle is:
options: Equal to the net heat absorbed in the cycle
Equal to $\Delta U$ of step $A \rightarrow B$
questions.solution:
For any complete cyclic process, the initial and final states are identical.
Since internal energy $U$ is a state function:
$$\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$$
By the First Law of Thermodynamics applied to the whole cycle:
$$\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = q_{\text{net}} + w_{\text{net}} = 0 \implies w_{\text{net}} = -q_{\text{net}}$$
Thus, the total net work done by the system is equal in magnitude to the net heat absorbed by the system.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] For which of the following reactions is $\Delta H = \Delta U$?
questions.solution:
From $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$, $\Delta H = \Delta U$ if and only if $\Delta n_g = 0$.
Evaluate $\Delta n_g = n_g(\text{products}) - n_g(\text{reactants})$ for each reaction:
- Option A: $2 - (1 + 1) = 2 - 2 = 0 \implies \Delta H = \Delta U$
- Option B: $2 - (1 + 3) = 2 - 4 = -2$
- Option C: $(1 + 1) - 1 = 2 - 1 = +1$
- Option D: $2 - 1 = +1$
Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U$ holds for $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{HI}(g)$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The heat of neutralization of a strong acid with a strong base in dilute aqueous solution at $298\text{ K}$ is $-57.1\text{ kJ/eq}$. When $0.5\text{ mole of HCl}$ is mixed with $0.2\text{ mole of NaOH}$, the heat evolved is:
questions.solution:
Neutralization reaction:
$$\text{H}^+(aq) + \text{OH}^-(aq) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l); \quad \Delta H = -57.1\text{ kJ/mol}$$
Moles of $\text{H}^+ = 0.5\text{ mol}$.
Moles of $\text{OH}^- = 0.2\text{ mol}$.
Here $\text{OH}^-$ is the limiting reagent, so only $0.2\text{ mole}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is formed.
Heat evolved:
$$q = 0.2\text{ mol} \times 57.1\text{ kJ/mol} = 11.42\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: Which of the following properties of a thermodynamic system is an intensive property?
questions.solution:
An intensive property is independent of the size or quantity of matter in the system.
- Volume, mass, internal energy, heat capacity, and enthalpy are extensive properties because they depend directly on the amount of substance.
- When an extensive property is divided by the mass or number of moles (e.g., molar heat capacity $C_{m} = C/n$, density $\rho = m/V$), it becomes an intensive property.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, the work done by the gas is $150\text{ J}$. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of the gas is:
questions.solution:
For an adiabatic process, there is no heat transfer:
$$q = 0$$
Work done by the gas means $w = -150\text{ J}$ (by IUPAC convention, expansion work is negative).
Applying the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = q + w = 0 + (-150\text{ J}) = -150\text{ J}$$
(The internal energy decreases because the gas does work at the expense of its own internal thermal energy).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Five moles of an ideal gas are compressed isothermally and reversibly at $27^\circ\text{C}$ from $1\text{ atm}$ to $10\text{ atm}$. The work done on the gas is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.303$)
questions.solution:
For an isothermal reversible compression:
$$w = -nRT \ln\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right) = +2.303 nRT \log_{10}\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)$$
Substitute $n = 5\text{ mol}$, $T = 27 + 273 = 300\text{ K}$, $P_1 = 1\text{ atm}$, $P_2 = 10\text{ atm}$:
$$w = 2.303 \times 5 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10}(10)$$
$$w = 2.303 \times 5 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 1 = 28721\text{ J} \approx +28.72\text{ kJ}$$
(Positive sign denotes work done on the system).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] For a reaction $\text{A}(s) + 2\text{B}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{C}(g) + \text{D}(s)$, $\Delta U^\circ = -10.5\text{ kJ}$ at $298\text{ K}$. The value of $\Delta H^\circ$ for the reaction is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Calculate $\Delta n_g$ for the reaction:
$$\Delta n_g = n_g(\text{products}) - n_g(\text{reactants}) = 2 - 2 = 0$$
Since $\Delta n_g = 0$:
$$\Delta H^\circ = \Delta U^\circ + \Delta n_g RT = \Delta U^\circ + 0 = -10.5\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The molar heat capacity at constant pressure ($C_p$) of an ideal gas is $\frac{7}{2}R$. The ratio of work done to the heat supplied at constant pressure during expansion is:
questions.solution:
At constant pressure:
- Heat supplied: $q_p = n C_p \Delta T = n\left(\frac{7}{2}R\right)\Delta T$
- Work done by the gas: $w_{\text{by}} = P \Delta V = n R \Delta T$
The ratio of work done to heat supplied is:
$$\frac{w_{\text{by}}}{q_p} = \frac{nR\Delta T}{n C_p \Delta T} = \frac{R}{C_p} = \frac{R}{\frac{7}{2}R} = \frac{2}{7}$$

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2023] Given the reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}(aq) + \text{NaOH}(aq) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa}(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l); \quad \Delta H = -55.8\text{ kJ/mol}$$
If the heat of neutralization of strong acid with strong base is $-57.3\text{ kJ/mol}$, the enthalpy of ionization of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is:
questions.solution:
The neutralization of a weak acid by a strong base involves two steps:
1) Ionization of weak acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+; \quad \Delta H_{\text{ion}}$
2) Neutralization of $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$: $\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}; \quad \Delta H_{\text{neut}} = -57.3\text{ kJ/mol}$

Total enthalpy of reaction:
$$\Delta H = \Delta H_{\text{ion}} + \Delta H_{\text{neut}}$$
$$-55.8 = \Delta H_{\text{ion}} - 57.3$$
$$\Delta H_{\text{ion}} = -55.8 + 57.3 = +1.5\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE concerning the First Law of Thermodynamics?
options: Energy of the universe remains conserved
In an isochoric process with no non-PV work, $q_v = \Delta U$
questions.solution:
By definition, an isolated system cannot exchange either matter or energy (heat or work) with its surroundings.
Therefore, for an isolated system, $q = 0$ and $w = 0$, which gives $\Delta U = 0$.
Statement A is false.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2022] For the reaction:
$$\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g)$$
If $\Delta U^\circ = 54.0\text{ kJ}$ at $300\text{ K}$, the value of $\Delta H^\circ$ is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Calculate $\Delta n_g$:
$$\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$$
Relation:
$$\Delta H^\circ = \Delta U^\circ + \Delta n_g RT$$
$$\Delta H^\circ = 54.0\text{ kJ} + \frac{1 \times 8.314 \times 300}{1000}\text{ kJ}$$
$$\Delta H^\circ = 54.0 + 2.4942 = 56.4942\text{ kJ} \approx 56.49\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a constant-volume bomb calorimeter, $1.0\text{ g}$ of a substance ($M = 100\text{ g/mol}$) is burned in excess oxygen. The temperature rises from $298.0\text{ K}$ to $300.0\text{ K}$. If the heat capacity of the calorimeter assembly is $10.0\text{ kJ/K}$, the heat of combustion at constant volume ($\Delta U_c$) per mole of the substance is:
questions.solution:
Heat evolved during the combustion in the bomb calorimeter:
$$q_{\text{cal}} = C_{\text{cal}} \Delta T = 10.0\text{ kJ/K} \times (300.0 - 298.0)\text{ K} = 10.0 \times 2.0 = 20.0\text{ kJ}$$
Heat produced by the system at constant volume:
$$q_v = -q_{\text{cal}} = -20.0\text{ kJ}$$
Moles of substance burned:
$$n = \frac{1.0\text{ g}}{100\text{ g/mol}} = 0.01\text{ mol}$$
Heat of combustion per mole:
$$\Delta U_c = \frac{q_v}{n} = \frac{-20.0\text{ kJ}}{0.01\text{ mol}} = -2000\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the work done (in Joules) when $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas expands isothermally from $1.0\text{ L}$ to $10.0\text{ L}$ against a constant opposing pressure of $1.0\text{ bar}$. (Take $1\text{ bar}\cdot\text{L} = 100\text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
For irreversible expansion against constant external pressure:
$$w = -P_{ext} (V_2 - V_1)$$
$$w = -1.0\text{ bar} \times (10.0 - 1.0)\text{ L} = -9.0\text{ bar}\cdot\text{L}$$
Convert to Joules:
$$w = -9.0 \times 100\text{ J} = -900.0\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] For the vaporization of water at $373\text{ K}$, $\Delta H_{\text{vap}} = 40.66\text{ kJ/mol}$. Find the change in internal energy $\Delta U_{\text{vap}}$ (in $\text{kJ/mol}$) for $1\text{ mole}$ of water. (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, round to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Phase transition:
$$\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$
$$\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = 1$$
Using $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$:
$$\Delta U = \Delta H - \Delta n_g RT$$
$$\Delta U = 40.66\text{ kJ/mol} - \frac{1 \times 8.314 \times 373}{1000}\text{ kJ/mol}$$
$$\Delta U = 40.66 - 3.101 = 37.559\text{ kJ/mol} \approx 37.56\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A gas absorbs $200\text{ J}$ of heat and undergoes expansion doing $120\text{ J}$ of work. Find the change in internal energy $\Delta U$ (in Joules).
questions.solution:
Heat absorbed by system: $q = +200\text{ J}$.
Work done by system: $w = -120\text{ J}$.
According to the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = q + w = 200 + (-120) = 80.0\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Enthalpy of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is $-393.5\text{ kJ/mol}$. Calculate the heat released (in kJ) upon formation of $35.2\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ from carbon and excess oxygen.
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 12 + 2(16) = 44\text{ g/mol}$.
Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ formed:
$$n = \frac{35.2\text{ g}}{44\text{ g/mol}} = 0.8\text{ mol}$$
Heat released for 1 mole formed $= 393.5\text{ kJ}$.
Heat released for $0.8\text{ mole}$:
$$q = 0.8 \times 393.5 = 314.8\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] For an ideal gas undergoing a reversible adiabatic process, if the initial temperature is $300\text{ K}$ and the volume expands to $8$ times its initial volume with $\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$, find the final temperature (in Kelvin).
questions.solution:
Using the adiabatic relation:
$$T_1 V_1^{\gamma - 1} = T_2 V_2^{\gamma - 1}$$
Given $\gamma = 5/3 \implies \gamma - 1 = 2/3$.
$$T_2 = T_1 \left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{\gamma - 1} = 300 \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{2/3}$$
Since $8^{2/3} = (2^3)^{2/3} = 2^2 = 4$:
$$T_2 = 300 \times \frac{1}{4} = 75.0\text{ K}$$
